subject: Post-call: Model fit & eval follow-up + regression concern
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Turner <lisa.turner@retailco.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Model fit & eval follow-up + regression concern

Thanks again for taking the time today, Lisa — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Summary of call: we reviewed your personalization use case (real-time product recommendations + short-form copy for promos), discussed latency SLOs (~150ms p50 target), cost targets, and tolerances for hallucination.
- Recommended models: for your mix of short-generation prompts + high-precision conditional outputs we recommend trying Redwood-7B-qa-quant and Redwood-13B-light for higher-quality fallbacks. See the evaluation deck attached.
- Benchmarks & prompt sets: shared a baseline eval in Drive and attached our recommended prompt_set_retailco_v2.jsonl. The Drive folder has per-model token counts, latency runs, and QA pass rates.
- Next steps (from Redwood):
  1) Provide the eval report and prompt sets (attached).
  2) Schedule a 30-min follow-up with engineering to review regression risk and pin/rollback strategy (cc'd Vivek + Rishi).
  3) We'll run a quick canary against a sample of your production traffic if you approve.

Attachments: retailco_eval_report_20260727.pdf, prompt_set_retailco_v2.jsonl

Open question: during the call you mentioned a spike in lower-quality outputs after a recent model update on your side. If you can share a couple of examples in reply, we'll prioritize that in the evaluation and propose pin/rollback options.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0127
https://redwood.com

From: Lisa Turner <lisa.turner@retailco.com>

Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit & eval follow-up + regression concern

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the summary and attachments. Quick follow-up:

We did notice a regression in the last weekly deployment (model v1.95 -> v1.96). Sample before/after (shortened):
- before (v1.95): "New arrivals include breathable linen shirts — perfect for summer."
- after (v1.96): "We have some shirts, maybe check?"

The drop in specificity/brand tone is visible across ~2-3% of prompts (our QA flagged it in the A/B test). We can share logs if useful — I attached a short snippet to this reply (pasted below).

I approve running your canary evaluation and would like pin/rollback options if the regression is confirmed. Also please include estimated impact to latency/cost for pinning to v1.95 vs staying on v1.96.

Thanks — Lisa
Director, Personalization | RetailCo
013 555 4321

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fwd: Post-call: Model fit & eval follow-up + regression concern

Vivek / Rishi — forwarding Lisa's note. She reports a measurable drop in copy specificity after we (or their side) moved from v1.95 -> v1.96. RetailCo is asking for: canary eval, diff of model changes, and a pin/rollback path (with latency/cost delta).

Can you:
1) Confirm whether v1.96 introduced any tokenization or decoding changes that could affect brevity/temperature.
2) Run the attached prompt set as a canary against v1.95 and v1.96 and produce a quick diff + recommended rollback/pin plan.
3) If rollback is advisable, propose a timeline (canary start, full rollback window) and any customer impact (latency, throughput changes).

I flagged this as high priority for the deal (HC-2026-078) — Lisa is hoping for a timeline today or tomorrow.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lisa Turner <lisa.turner@retailco.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: Model fit & eval follow-up + regression concern

Thanks for the heads-up, Marissa — quick engineering readout below after an initial pass.

What we did:
- Ran the attached prompt_set_retailco_v2.jsonl on both model snapshots (v1.95 and v1.96) in a controlled canary environment.
- Computed simple QA pass-rate and semantic similarity deltas (see short summary).

Findings (TL;DR):
- v1.96 shows a 2.8% drop in QA pass-rate on copy-specific prompts and a measurable decrease in BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics for short-format promotional text.
- No tokenization changes between the snapshots; the diffs point to a changed decoding default (temperature scheduling + beam fallback) and a small change in cached attention normalization that appears to favor brevity in specific contexts.

Recommended remediation options:
A) Pin to v1.95 for RetailCo (fastest path):
   - Impact: mitigates regression, expected to restore prior quality. Minimal latency delta (~+5ms p50) and negligible cost delta.
   - Rollback plan: Canary pin for 12 hours (5% traffic), validate QA pass-rate, then full rollback over 1 hour.
B) Patch v1.96 (medium path):
   - Engineering tweak to decoding defaults and attention norm. Estimated ETA: 3 business days to implement + 1 day of canary.
C) Long-term: add a model gating rule for generation-sensitive routes to prefer v1.95 family unless manually overridden.

Attachments: diff_patch_v1.95-1.96.txt (contains short code diff + notes), drive link to per-prompt diffs: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/retailco-evals-2026-07

Permission asked: Marissa / Lisa, shall we proceed with option A (immediate pin to v1.95 with 12hr canary)? If yes, we can schedule canary start within 2 hours and will report back with pass-rate after the canary window.

-Vivek
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Lisa
